label: International Space Station (cabin)
notes: Sea-level air: NASA's OCHMO technical brief states the ISS cabin is 'typically maintained at 14.7 psia with 21% O2' (14.7 psia = 101.3 kPa). Ventilation band 5-20 cm/s is an EMBER engineering assumption: NASA sources describe spacecraft ventilation as 'of the order of 0.1 m/s' (NTRS 19990053973) and 'a few centimeters per second' (NTRS 20050199446); NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 2 [V2 6107] only requires circulation that prevents CO2 and thermal pockets, without a numeric velocity.

label: Crew capsule in transit (Orion-class)
notes: Modeled as sea-level air like ISS. We did not find a NASA page that states Orion's nominal Artemis cabin O2/pressure numerically, so the values are an assumption. Context from NASA: Orion was once designed for 'up to 30% oxygen at a pressure of 10.2 psia for lunar missions' and its materials are certified at 30% O2 / 10.2 psia; at 14.7 psia the cabin O2 'cannot be set higher than 25.6%' without potentially invalidating that certification (NTRS 20090012334). Shuttle also flew 10.2 psia / 26.5% O2 during staged EVA prep (NTRS 20240003211).

label: Lunar surface habitat (exploration atmosphere)
notes: NASA's recommended exploration atmosphere for EVA-intensive lunar surface habitats: 8.2 psia (56.5 kPa) / 34% O2 (revised from 8.0 psia / 32%). NASA notes the final specification is still being evaluated and that fire management in this oxygen-enriched atmosphere is an open challenge; a 2026 NASA paper reports a team recommendation of an 'alternate vehicle atmosphere' for early surface missions (NTRS 20260002050) and NASA chamber tests used an 'alternate exploration atmosphere' of 66.2 kPa / 28.5% O2 (NTRS 20240013238). Ventilation band is an assumption (see iss).

label: Pressurized lunar rover
notes: 30% O2 at 10.2 psia (70.3 kPa) is the worst-case condition NASA uses to certify spacecraft materials for lunar missions ('all materials are certified in the 30% oxygen, 10.2 psia environment', NTRS 20090012334) and the lunar-base / rover condition given in the Space Apps challenge brief (per EMBER_concept.md). NASA has not published a rover cabin atmosphere specification that we could find, so this is a design scenario, not a NASA rover spec. Lower flow bound 0 cm/s represents a fan-off / quiescent cabin (crews turn ventilation off to fight a fire, NTRS 20050217475).

label: Mars surface habitat
notes: NASA states that future missions to the Moon and Mars 'are expected to use nitrox gas mixtures of up to 34% O2, 66% N2' and recommends the 56.5 kPa / 34% exploration atmosphere (NTRS 20220009536). No Mars-specific habitat atmosphere has been fixed, so EMBER treats the lunar exploration atmosphere as the Mars scenario. Ventilation band is an assumption.

label: EVA spacesuit (pure O2)
notes: The ISS EVA suit is 'pressurized to 4.3 psi' (29.6 kPa) and filled with pure oxygen (OCHMO-TB-003; NASA podcast). Prebreathe protocols use 95% O2 and NASA tested planetary EVAs at 29.6 or 35.6 kPa (NTRS 20240013238), so ~100% O2 is an approximation. Gravity set to lunar (Artemis surface EVA); for ISS EVAs use 0 g. Suit ventilation velocity is not given in the sources we found (null).
